Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results Emeryville, CA – November 10, 2026 – Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. (NASDAQ: GO) ("Grocery Outlet," the "Company," "we" or "our") today announced financial results for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 ended October 3, 2026. Highlights for Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 as compared to the Prior Year Period: • Net sales increased by 0.9% to $1.18 billion. • Comparable store sales increased by 0.5%. • Gross margin was 30.0% compared to 30.4% last y ear . • Operating income was $24.0 million , whic h included $3.6 million in net res tructuring credits. • Net income was $13.3 million, or $0.13 per diluted share, compared to $11.6 million, or $0.12 per diluted share last year. Adjusted net income (1) was $15.6 million, or $0.16 diluted adjusted earnings per share (1) , compared to $20.7 million, or $0.21 diluted adjusted earnings per share (1) last year. • Adjusted EBITDA (1) was $59.4 million, representing 5.0% of net sales. Highlights for the 39 Weeks Ended October 3, 2026 as compared to the Prior Year Period: • Net sales increased by 1.8% to $3.54 billion. • Comparable store sales declined by 0.2%. • Gross margin was 29.9% compared to 30.5% last year. • Operating loss was $138.2 million, which included $158.0 million in non-cash goodwill impairment and $20.1 million in net restructuring charges. • Net loss was $161.4 million, or $(1.63) per diluted share, compared to net loss of $6.8 million, or $(0.07) per diluted share last year. Adjusted net income (1) was $40.5 million, or $0.41 diluted adjusted earnings per share (1) , compared to $56.5 million, or $0.57 diluted adjusted earnings per share (1) last year. • Adjusted EBITDA (1) was $168.2 million, representing 4.8% of net sales. “In the third quarter we returned to positive comparable store sales, driven by continued improvements to the execution of our opportunistic product offering,” said Jason Potter, President and CEO of Grocery Outlet. “Traffic accelerated and basket trends again improved sequentially as we enhanced our value proposition. In partnership with our operators and suppliers, we will continue to build on this progress with a focus on driving sustainable sales growth and improved profitability over time. This stronger foundation increases our confidence in our long-term opportunity.” __________________________________ (1) Adjusted net income, diluted adjusted earnings per share, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin are non-GAAP financial measures, which exclude the impact of certain special items. Please note that our non-GAAP financial measures should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. See the "Non-GAAP Financial Information" section of this release as well as the respective reconciliations of our non-GAAP financial measures below for additional information about these items. 1 Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Summary Net sales increased 0.9% to $1.18 billion due to new store sales and a 0.5% increase in comparable store sales, partially offset by decreased sales from store closures as a result of the Optimization Plan as further discussed below. The increase in comparable store sales was driven by a 2.4% increase in the number of transactions, partially offset by a 1.9% decrease in average transaction size. We opened 14 new stores and closed zero stores, ending the quarter with 561 stores in 16 states. Gross profit decreased slightly to $353.0 million. Gross margin was 30.0%, a decline of 40 basis points due primarily to the impact of product promotions to drive sales, higher transportation expenses, and the impact from a broad reduction in consumer demand for produce as a result of a Cyclospora outbreak associated with certain fresh produce items, partially offset by a favorable shift in sales mix toward opportunistic products. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased slightly to $332.5 million. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses declined 10 basis points to 28.2%. Operating income was $24.0 million, which included $3.6 million in net restructuring credits related to the Optimization Plan consisting of $15.8 million in non-cash credits primarily from the net write-off of lease right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, partially offset by $12.2 million in cash charges. 39 Weeks Ended October 3, 2026 Financial Summary Net sales increased 1.8% to $3.54 billion due to new store sales, partially offset by decreased sales from store closures as a result of the Optimization Plan and a 0.2% decrease in comparable store sales. The decrease in comparable store sales was driven by a 2.3% decrease in average transaction size, partially offset by a 2.1% increase in the number of transactions. We opened 31 new stores and closed 40 stores, including 36 stores as a result of the Optimization Plan. Gross profit was relatively unchanged at $1.06 billion. Gross margin decreased 60 basis points to 29.9% during the first three quarters, driven primarily by the impact of product promotions to drive sales, inventory markdowns and write-offs associated with the store closures under the Optimization Plan, and higher transportation expenses, partially offset by improvements in inventory management. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by 2.0% versus last year to $1.02 billion. As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses were relatively unchanged at 28.8% during the first three quarters. Operating loss was $138.2 million, which included a $158.0 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge during the first quarter of fiscal 2026 as a result of a decline in stock price, and $20.1 million in net restructuring charges related to the Optimization Plan consisting of $29.7 million in cash charges, partially offset by $9.6 million in net non-cash credits primarily from the net write-off of lease right-of-use assets and lease liabilities. The non-cash goodwill impairment charge does not impact future operations. Cash Flow & Capital Spending: • Net cash provided by operating activities during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $18.2 million compared with $17.3 million for the third quarter last year. The increase in operating cash flow was driven primarily by higher accrued and other liabilities due primarily to timing, partially offset by lower operating lease liabilities as a result of the Optimization Plan. 2 • Capital expenditures for the third quarter of fiscal 2026, before tenant improvement allowances, were $28.1 million, a decrease of $16.3 million from the third quarter of fiscal 2025 due to lower spending on current and future new store openings and prior year investments in new warehouses. Capital expenditures, net of tenant improvement allowances, for the third quarter this year, were $25.7 million compared with $39.4 million for the same period last year. Optimization Plan: As previously reported, we initiated a business optimization plan during the first quarter of fiscal 2026, intended to strengthen long-term profitability and cash flow generation, improve operational execution, optimize our existing store footprint and align with our disciplined new store growth strategy (the "Optimization Plan"). Under the Optimization Plan, we closed 36 financially underperforming stores ("Closure Stores") in March and April of 2026. We have negotiated, or intend to negotiate, the termination, sublease or assignment of the store leases for the Closure Stores. In addition, we have substantially completed the termination of operator agreements with independent operators for the Closure Stores and certain other store locations (the "Operator Agreement Terminations"). Yesway, Inc. (“Yesway” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: YSWY), one of the fastest-growing convenience store operators
in the United States, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights · Net income increased to $24.8 million from $15.9
million in the prior-year period, and Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.6% year-over-year to $59.6 million. · Same-store inside merchandise sales increased
1.9% year-over-year. Total inside merchandise sales increased 4.0% year-over-year, with a total inside merchandise margin of 35.1%. · Same-store fuel gallons sold increased 1.1% year-over-year.

of Yesway. “We continued to grow inside merchandise sales and fuel gallons, expand our market share, and deliver strong profitability
against a challenging consumer environment. This continued momentum reflects our differentiated market positioning, deliberate geographic
focus, significant diesel exposure, and destination foodservice platform.” Mr. Trkla continued, “We are proud
of what our team has accomplished and excited for what is ahead for Yesway as we continue to advance our three growth priorities –
new store development, initiatives that strengthen our existing operations, and selective acquisitions – and drive long-term value

EX-99.1 3 pphcannouncesnew105milli.htm EX-99.1 pphcannouncesnew105milli PPHC Announces New $105 Million Senior Secured Credit Facility November 2, 2026 Five-year facility refinances existing borrowings and provides additional capacity to support acquisitions and general corporate purposes WASHINGTON,  Nov.  02,  2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)  --  Public  Policy  Holding  Company,  Inc.  ("PPHC",  the  "Group"  or  the "Company") (Nasdaq: PPHC), a leading global strategic communications provider offering a comprehensive range of advisory services in Government Relations, Public Affairs and Corporate Communications, announces that it has entered into a new $105 million senior secured credit facility with a U.S. commercial bank (the “New Facility”). The New Facility  comprises  a  $65 million  term loan  and  a  $40  million  revolving  credit  facility.  The Group intends  to  seek commitments from additional lenders through a syndication to increase the New Facility to an aggregate $150 million. The New Facility  may include an additional  uncommitted accordion option of  up to $50 million.  Syndication is  being undertaken on a best-efforts basis and is currently anticipated to close in January 2027. Key Terms A five-year senior secured facility comprising a $65 million term loan and a $40 million revolving credit facility at initial closing. Expected syndication to a total facility size of $150 million, anticipated to close in January 2027 on a best-efforts basis. An uncommitted accordion option of up to an additional $50 million, subject to lender approval and the satisfaction of applicable conditions. Interest payable at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus a margin of 185 to 230 basis points, determined by the Group’s net leverage ratio.  An unused commitment fee of 15 to 25 basis points applies to undrawn revolving commitments, also based on net leverage. Term loan amortization, stated as a percentage of the original balance, of 5.0% in each of years one and two, 7.5% in each of years three and four, and 10.0% in year five, with the remaining balance due at maturity on November 2, 2031. The revolving credit facility is interest only. Secured by a blanket lien over the Group’s assets, with guarantees from substantially all subsidiaries. Use of Proceeds The proceeds of the New Facility will be used to refinance the Group’s existing debt, fund acquisitions including an immediate drawdown to  fund the initial  cash consideration for  the acquisition of  Reevemark LLC announced earlier  today and provide additional capacity for working capital and general corporate purposes. Existing Facilities The Group’s existing borrowings under the credit arrangements first announced on March 1, 2023, and subsequently expanded and amended on April 30, 2024, June 6, 2024, and January 24, 2025, will be repaid and replaced by the New Facility shortly after closing. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $39.8 million was outstanding under the existing facilities. Capital Allocation The New Facility consolidates the Group’s borrowings into a single financing structure on more favorable terms, extends the Group’s debt maturity profile, and provides additional capacity to support its growth strategy. The Group intends to maintain a prudent leverage ratio as it combines organic growth with targeted, earnings-accretive M&A. The PPHC Board of Directors considers that access to both debt and equity funding provides appropriate flexibility in the Group’s capital allocation, including the funding of acquisitions and deferred consideration, as well as the payment of dividends. Stewart Hall, CEO of PPHC, commented: “This  new  facility  strengthens  our  financial  position  and  provides  additional  capacity  to  execute  our  growth  strategy  while maintaining a disciplined approach to leverage and capital allocation. We remain focused on deploying capital selectively into opportunities that enhance our capabilities, broaden our geographic reach and create long-term value for shareholders.” B/T Advisory acted as exclusive debt advisor, and Venable LLP acted as legal counsel to the Group. Further details of the New Facility, including the identity of the lender and a copy of the credit agreement, will be set out in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which will  be available at www.sec.gov and on the Company’s investor relations website. About PPHC Incorporated in 2014, PPHC is a global strategic communications platform that supports clients in enhancing and defending their reputations,  advancing  policy  objectives,  managing  regulatory  risk,  and  engaging  with  federal  and  state-level  policymakers, stakeholders, media, and the public. Engaged by approximately 1,500 clients, including companies, trade associations and non-governmental organizations, PPHC is active in  all  major  sectors  of  the economy,  including healthcare and pharmaceuticals,  financial  services,  energy,  technology, telecommunications and transportation. With operations across 18 offices in the United States and internationally, PPHC's services include government relations, public affairs  and  corporate  communications,  research  and  analytics,  digital  advocacy  campaigning,  and  compliance  support. EX-99.1 2 arwr-202611048kex991.htm EX-99.1 Document EXHIBIT 99.1 PRESS RELEASE November 4 , 2026 Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Refinances Existing Credit Facility, Lowering Borrowing Costs and Extending Maturity – Existing $400 million facility prepaid at a $68 million discount to the contractual minimum repayment amount – New $400 million term loan priced at SOFR plus 5.50% – Debt has no scheduled amortization payments or required sweeps during the term prior to the Maturity Date of November 2, 2031 PASADENA, Calif., November 4, 2026 — Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today announced that it has completed a refinancing with funds managed by Sixth Street that lowers its borrowing costs, improves near-term liquidity, extends its debt maturity, and increases financial and operational flexibility. The transaction retires Arrowhead’s existing $400 million Sixth Street facility at a $68 million discount to the contractual minimum repayment amount and establishes a new $400 million Sixth Street senior secured term loan facility bearing interest at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 5.50%. “This transaction is an important step in aligning our capital structure with the company Arrowhead has become. By reducing the amount required to retire our existing facility and lowering our ongoing borrowing costs, we are improving the economics of our financing for shareholders,” said Daniel Apel, MBA, CPA, Chief Financial Officer of Arrowhead. “As we build the REDEMPLO® business and advance our pipeline, we are securing financing terms that more closely reflect our profile as a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company. Sixth Street’s continued support reflects its confidence in our business and the opportunities ahead.” Transaction Highlights • Lower borrowing costs. The new facility carries an interest rate of SOFR plus 5.50%, compared to an annual rate of 15% in the retired facility. • Reduced minimum prepayment multiple. Negotiated a $68 million discount on the contractual prepayment amount on the retired facility, which originally carried a minimum 2x multiple on invested capital (MOIC) if paid in full by August 2028 and escalated to a 2.5x MOIC thereafter. • Reduced contractual sweep obligation. The retired facility required Arrowhead to partially repay loans under the credit facility with a sweep of a portion of the proceeds from certain transactions, such as the future collection of upfront payments, milestones, and royalties from partnerships and collaborations, and commercial revenue by Arrowhead. The new facility eliminates these required prepayments or sweeps and reduces the prepayment premiums associated with paying off the facility early. • Greater strategic, financial, and operational flexibility. The new facility significantly improves Arrowhead’s ability to independently engage in strategic, financial, and operational activities. • Extended maturity enhancing near-term liquidity. The new facility matures in November 2031. “Arrowhead has made significant progress in translating its RNAi platform into a commercial business with substantial growth opportunities,” said Jeff Pootoolal, Partner, and Michael Reslinski, Managing Director at Sixth Street. “We are pleased to continue our relationship through a new financing structure that recognizes that progress and supports the company’s next phase of growth.” The new senior secured credit facility matures on November 2, 2031, and bears interest at an annual rate equal to the 3-month SOFR plus 5.50%, with certain additional fees and prepayment terms. There are no scheduled amortization payments during the term of the facility, with all principal due on the maturity date. Arrowhead is not required to prepay or sweep any proceeds from certain transactions, such as the future collection of upfront payments, milestones, and royalties from partnerships and collaborations, and commercial revenue. Arrowhead may prepay all or any portion of the loans at any time at a prespecified premium, not to exceed 2%, if prepaid more than 18 months after the Closing Date, plus a make-whole premium for any prepayments made prior to May 2, 2028. All obligations will be secured on a first-priority basis, subject to certain exceptions, by security interests in substantially all assets of the company.
